title: Exact Thinking in Demented Times: The Vienna Circle and the Epic Quest for the Foundations of Science
author: Karl Sigmund
note: Selected for Erwin Dekker's strong praise of the narrative and scientific explanations, corroborating MAA reception, and Goodreads 4.15/633. Dekker's substantial criticism of the underdeveloped political interpretation and unsympathetic treatment of Neurath is retained. This is a historical group biography, not an endorsement of logical positivism as established truth or a technical logic curriculum. Criticism of the historical subjects' philosophy does not itself veto the biography. The inspected critique limits the synthesis but does not establish high-confidence foundational failure of the historical account. Philosophy is central, so T12 applies. Vienna is the setting but the international scientific movement and its dispersal are the subject, so T11=0. Original German publication was 2015; English translation does not reset P14.
notes: Documented intellectual history, with limitations in political framing identified by Dekker.
Connects scientific foundations, mathematical work, intellectual networks and political disruption.
Useful cases of interdisciplinary collaboration and competing standards of explanation.
Explains intellectual developments more fully than institutional and political causation.

D=7.5, moderate confidence from Dekker's detailed review, contents and reader reports. Scientific ideas and contrasting figures add value; personal episodes and underdeveloped political synthesis limit yield. No full-text audit.
Scientific organization and epistemic debates remain durable.
Direct mathematics and philosophy-of-science relevance; limited production or engineering content.
Established mathematician writing a documented historical synthesis.
Clear, well-integrated group narrative, strongly praised by Dekker.
Accessible scientific explanations with occasional rhetorical framing.
